title: x-rail ticket payload
description:
The decoded payload of the `x-rail` header — what Rail Center mints, as the thing an enforcement point reads. The header itself is urlsafe-base64 of this object, with no `Bearer` prefix and padding optional.

This is the *payload* contract. How to decode the header safely, how to classify what comes out, and what a claim resolving to absent means are the *reading* contract, and are deliberately not restated here: an implementation validating a payload against this schema has not thereby read a ticket correctly. In particular this schema describes a ticket the mint produced, and a reader must handle ones it did not — the forged, the truncated and the expired.

Wave 1 tickets are unsigned. Anyone able to construct JSON can produce one that satisfies this schema, so conformance here is a statement about shape and never about authenticity.

agent_id.description: The agent this ticket is for, assigned by Rail Center at registration. `format` is an annotation in draft 2020-12 and most validators do not check it, so a reader that needs the id to be a UUID must say so itself.

sandbox_id.description: Derived identity: sha256(json(["host-identity", host_id, sandbox_name]))[:16] when the pair is known, else a hostname-derived fallback.

environment_fingerprint.description: sha256(sandbox_type:llm_provider:llm_model:skills_hash)[:16]. Changes when the agent's environment does.

sandbox_type.description: For example nemo_claw, kubernetes, bare_metal. Not an enumeration: a deployment may name a sandbox this schema has never heard of, and refusing it here would make an agent that registers cleanly impossible to admit.

posture_score.description: null until scoring has run, and always null on the ticket that agent registration returns. A number here is a score, never a string: the evaluation contract's ordered operators compare numbers only, so "30" does not satisfy `lt 40`.

tier.description: trusted at 80 or above, caution at 60, elevated_risk at 40, critical below. null until scored. Left unconstrained rather than enumerated for the same reason as sandbox_type — the bands are Rail Center's to change, and a reader that refused an unfamiliar one would deny an agent whose score is perfectly readable.

skills.description: Declared skill names, read by the skill_match derived field. An empty list is a present claim, not a missing one.

scored_at.description: When posture was last computed. Not a lifetime — that is exp.

iat.description: Issued at: whole seconds since the Unix epoch, UTC.

exp.description: Expires at, in the same units. The ticket is dead *at* exp, not one second after. Bounded by ±(2^53 − 1) because JSON has no integer type: past that a double cannot separate adjacent integers, and two readers would take different instants from the same bytes.
